metadata.title: Exploration Licenses (Istrazne Dozvole) for Mining and Mineral Resources in Serbia
metadata.title_sr: Istrazne dozvole za rudarstvo i mineralne sirovine u Srbiji
metadata.description: Comprehensive registry of active, pending, and recently expired exploration licenses on Serbian territory. Data compiled from Ministry of Mining and Energy publications, company filings (ASX, TSX, LSE), investor presentations, and news sources.
metadata.note: Serbia has approximately 172 active exploration fields covering ~1,100,000 hectares (~1/8 of national territory). About a dozen companies from Australia, Canada, and China control ~90% of the territory permitted for metallic ore exploration.
metadata.coordinate_system: WGS84 (EPSG:4326). Serbian national system uses Gauss-Kruger Zone 7 (EPSG:4075/8684/8685). Polygon coordinates where available are approximate and derived from investor presentations, not official cadastre data.
data_sources: Serbian Ministry of Mining and Energy (Ministarstvo rudarstva i energetike) - mre.gov.rs
Serbian Geological Survey (Geoloski zavod Srbije - GRAS)
ASX company announcements and investor presentations
TSX/TSXV company filings and NI 43-101 technical reports
BRGM Mineral Deposits and Mining Districts of Serbia GIS Database

legal_framework.governing_law: Law on Mining and Geological Explorations (Zakon o rudarstvu i geoloskim istrazivanjima)
legal_framework.issuing_authority: Ministry of Mining and Energy (for most of Serbia) / Autonomous Province of Vojvodina (for Vojvodina territory)
legal_framework.exploration_permit_duration_years: up to 3 years initial, extendable to 8 years total
legal_framework.area_specification: Defined by coordinates in national coordinate system on topographic map 1:25,000, limited to not more than two closed polygons
legal_framework.cadastre: Ministry maintains cadastre of exploration spaces and exploitation spaces (Article 161 of the Law)

exploration_licenses.notes: Cukaru Peki Upper Zone in production since 2021. Lower Zone under development. Combined 2025 guidance: 290,000t Cu and 7t Au.

royalty_holders.note: Over portions of Jasikovo-Durlan Potok exploration license north of Bor Mine

exploration_licenses.notes: Located north of the currently active Bor Mine. Part of the greater Bor Mining District exploration portfolio.

royalty_holders.note: ~700m west of Cukaru Peki. Contains Corridor Zone high-grade gold prospect.

exploration_licenses.notes: Immediately adjacent and to the west of the Brestovac Mining License and Cukaru Peki Mine.

exploration_licenses.stock_exchange: LSE: RIO, ASX: RIO, NYSE: RIO
key_deposits: Jadar deposit - only known occurrence of jadarite mineral
exploration_licenses.date_issued: 2004 (initial discovery); various dates for subsequent permits
exploration_licenses.notes: One of the largest lithium deposits in the world. Project was halted in 2022 when spatial plan was revoked. Constitutional Court ruled revocation unconstitutional in July 2024. Project resumed then suspended again in late 2025 due to permitting delays. Currently on care and maintenance. Corporate history: formerly Jadar Lithium Beograd, Centurion Metals, Nova Centauri Metals - ultimately controlled by Rio Tinto Minerals Development Limited (London).

exploration_licenses.license_holder: DPM Avala d.o.o. / Dunav Minerals d.o.o.
exploration_licenses.parent_company: DPM Metals Inc. (formerly Dundee Precious Metals Inc.)

coka_rakita.note: High-grade gold deposit. PFS shows $735M NPV at 5%. Drill intercepts: 40m at 63.6 g/t Au.

exploration_licenses.notes: Originally acquired via Avala Resources (TSX.V: AVZ, acquired April 2016) and Dunav Resources. DPM operates through DPM Avala and Dunav Minerals, both owned by Dundee Precious Avala SARL (Luxembourg). Total area ~40,000 hectares. Coka Rakita feasibility study expected late 2025, first production targeted 2028. In September 2025, DPM completed acquisition of Adriatic Metals for $1.3B, adding Serbian Raska assets.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: DPM Metals Inc. (via Adriatic Metals acquisition)
exploration_licenses.project_name: Raska Project (formerly Adriatic Metals Raska Project)
exploration_licenses.notes: Past-producing Zn-Pb-Ag open pit mines. Located 280 km south of Belgrade and 20 km north of Raska town. On the Tethyan Metallogenic Belt. Acquired by DPM through Adriatic Metals acquisition completed September 2025.

exploration_licenses.project_name: Rogozna Gold and Base Metals Project
exploration_licenses.notes: Located ~400km south of Belgrade near Novi Pazar in the Trepca Mineral District. Within the Tethyan Metallogenic Belt. Mining heritage dating to Roman times. Yugoslav Geological Survey identified significant Pb-Zn-Ag reserves in 20th century. Previous explorers: Freeport, Eldorado Gold. Strickland acquired from Ibaera Capital in 2024. Planning 70,000m drill campaign in 2026.
Approval received from Ministry of Mining and Energy for maiden drill programme. IP geophysical survey completed to refine drill targets. Permit extendable beyond 2028.

Granted license. Located 60km from Cukaru Peki deposit. Within the Tethyan Magmatic Belt. Acquired from Apollo Minerals. Massive antimony sulphide (stibnite) confirmed. Historical antimony content up to 4.5% and 2.7% Sb.
Tenure in application. Acquired from Apollo Minerals. Area of former Lisa Mines with high-grade antimony mining history.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Erin Ventures Inc. / Temas Resources Corp. (JV)
exploration_licenses.notes: License granted by Serbian Ministry of Mining and Energy. Temas has option to earn 50% equity by spending EUR 10.5M over 36 months. Located in historical mining region with excellent infrastructure, 250 km south of Belgrade. Updated PEA commissioned. Advancing licensing process toward exploitation.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Electrum Discovery Corp. (formerly Medgold Resources Corp.)
exploration_licenses.project_name: Tlamino Gold Project (part of Novo Tlamino)
exploration_licenses.notes: Part of original Tlamino Project. Near Bosilegrad, within Donje Tlamino license. Five hours south of Belgrade. Close to Bulgarian and Macedonian borders.

exploration_licenses.project_name: Tlamino Gold Project (part of Novo Tlamino)
exploration_licenses.notes: Part of original Tlamino Project. Contiguous with Donje Tlamino. Combined two licenses total 192 km2.
Seven license portfolio expanding Tlamino project footprint. Total 522 km2.

Located on eastern margin of Timok Magmatic Complex. Bambino anomaly <5km from Bor Mine. Selected for BHP's 2025 Xplor Accelerator Programme (up to US$500,000 in non-dilutive funding). Spring 2025 field program launched with geological mapping, geophysical surveys, geochemical sampling.
Located on northern flank of Kopaonik metallogenic zone. Granted by Serbian Ministry of Energy and Mines. Epithermal gold and porphyry copper targets confirmed.
Part of Terra Balcanica's total Serbian portfolio of 130.36 km2. Second largest mineral exploration license holder in the Raska district.

Ministry refused renewal because Euro Lithium failed to complete required 75% of exploration works. Strong local opposition - residents from villages around Valjevo blocked roads and prevented exploration activities (April 2024). ELB+ cornerstone asset.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Elemental Royalty Corp. (optioned to BHP Group Ltd.)
exploration_licenses.notes: One of three licenses optioned to BHP (January 2026). Lies directly south of Zijin's Brestovac license, covering extension of geologic trend hosting Cukaru Peki and Malka Golaja deposits. BHP can earn 100% by spending $5M over 5 years. Elemental retains 2% NSR royalty.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Elemental Royalty Corp. (optioned to BHP Group Ltd.)
exploration_licenses.notes: Second of three licenses optioned to BHP (January 2026). Part of the same geologic trend as Lenovac North.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Elemental Royalty Corp. (optioned to BHP Group Ltd.)
exploration_licenses.notes: Third of three licenses optioned to BHP (January 2026). Contains stratigraphic sections hosting Coka Marin and Coka Rakita skarn. Elemental's total Serbian portfolio covers over 150 km2 along trend of major Bor District deposits.
Central portion of Timok Magmatic Complex. Directly west of established Bor Mine. BHP drilling commenced summer 2025. Part of larger Borsko project area (~40 km2).

Northern portion of Timok Magmatic Complex, directly north of Majdanpek Mine Complex. BHP earning interest and providing sole funding. Five prospective porphyry targets advanced. SouthWest Zone <2km NW of Majdanpek deposit. Drilling at North Central target commenced Sept 2025, first hole reached 900m depth.

resources.tilva_rosh_south_trenching: 12m at 30.39 g/t Au and 171.27 g/t Ag

exploration_licenses.notes: Option agreement with BHP for 7 exploration licenses. BHP can earn 100% by funding US$35M in exploration over 10 years. Mundoro retains 2% NSR royalty. Joint technical working group established to integrate historical datasets. Priority targets: Tilva Rosh and Skorusa (H1 2026).

individual_licenses.name: Savinac
individual_licenses.note: 15km SW of Bor Mine. Contains Tilva Rosh prospect.

individual_licenses.name: Osnic
individual_licenses.note: 20km south of Bor Mine Complex in NE Serbia.

exploration_licenses.notes: Four contiguous licenses covering southern extension of Timok Magmatic Complex. BHP commenced 2,500m drill program. Located 40-70 km south of Bor Mine Complex.
Part of Mundoro's broader Serbian portfolio. Expenditures maintained for calendar 2015 onward.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (via Balkan istrazivanja d.o.o. Beograd)
exploration_licenses.parent_company: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (formerly Bayan Mining and Minerals)

resources.note: First two diamond drill holes (1,238m) revealed preserved lithium and borate mineralization at both sites.

exploration_licenses.notes: Flagship project. Three contiguous exploration licenses near Jagodina and Kragujevac in Pomoravlje district. Survey area 175 km2 covers almost half of Rekovac municipality territory (366 km2). Significant local opposition - municipal assembly amended spatial plan to try to block activities.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (via subsidiary)
exploration_licenses.notes: Expansion licenses providing extension of Rekovac project. Originally secured by Jadar Lithium/Jadar Resources.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (via subsidiary)
exploration_licenses.notes: Part of Cacak project area. Favorable lacustrine strata for hosting lithium and boron. Within the lithium-borate Vardar belt.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (via subsidiary)
exploration_licenses.notes: Part of Cacak project area. Within the lithium-borate Vardar belt. Favorable lacustrine strata.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Boron One Holdings Inc. (via Balkan Gold d.o.o.)

resources.note: 3 of 6 drill holes intersected borates exceeding economic criteria for grade and thickness.

exploration_licenses.notes: Located 250 km south of Belgrade. Jarandol Basin is a historical mining district with two known boron deposits, an operating coal mine, and a depleted magnesite mine. Basin has hosted mining for 100+ years with excellent infrastructure. 2024-25 exploration program completed. Annual Report submitted to Ministry of Mining.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Middle Island Resources Limited (via Konstantin Resources acquisition)
exploration_licenses.license_area_name: Bobija Project (6 licenses: Bobija, Bobija East, Kamenita Kosa + 3 mineral licenses)
exploration_licenses.notes: Largest mineral exploration license holder in Serbia with 14 licenses covering 62,000 hectares (620 km2). Acquired via Konstantin Resources in 2025. Exploration commenced with large-scale polymetallic targets identified.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Middle Island Resources Limited (via Konstantin Resources)
exploration_licenses.notes: One granted license (Brodica) and four applications.

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Middle Island Resources Limited (via Konstantin Resources)
exploration_licenses.notes: Three granted exploration licenses. Underexplored copper discovery within highly-mineralized corridor. Hosts Cadinje Cu-Au skarn deposit to the SE.

License application covering low gravity field in north of Jadar basin on Pannonian plain. 10-25km west of Sabac. Neighbours Rio Tinto's Jadar lithium-borate project. Limited exploration already identified presence of lithium and borate. Railways and major roads nearby.
Serbian domestic company with exploration rights for lithium and boron.
State-owned public enterprise for underground coal exploitation. Established 2003. Operates 9 mines. Produces >500,000 tonnes of high quality coal annually. 3,529 employees (2023).

exploration_licenses.license_holder: Balkan Mining and Minerals Limited (via subsidiary)
exploration_licenses.notes: One of Balkan Mining and Minerals' additional Serbian licenses alongside Rekovac, Ursule, Siokovac, Dobrinja, and Pranjani. Near Pozega, where locals expressed opposition to lithium research.

resources.drill_intercepts: 40m at 63.6 g/t Au, 73m at 43.36 g/t Au and 0.12% Cu

exploration_licenses.notes: Located 3km SE of Timok gold project and ~35km NW of Bor. 109 km2 project area. Easy access to roads, power lines and technical support. Feasibility study expected late 2025, construction potentially mid-2026, first concentrate production 2028. PFS shows $735M NPV at 5% and 41% IRR.

key_deposits: Over 90 separate ore bodies within license area
exploration_licenses.notes: Historic mine on Mount Rudnik, active since Roman times. Exploitation license of 4.4 km2. Revenue approximately $70.6M.

exploration_licenses.parent_company: Formerly Nevsun/Freeport JV, now part of Zijin orbit
exploration_licenses.notes: Three exploration permits totaling 212.58 km2. Brestovac-Metovnica is one of three. Located 5km south of Bor town. Originally a Nevsun-Freeport JV. Exploration on both Cukaru Peki and Lower Zone.

minerals_explored.copper: Most common target, primarily in Timok/Bor region
minerals_explored.gold: Second most common, often co-targeted with copper
minerals_explored.lithium: Growing interest in western/central Serbia (Jadar basin, Vardar belt)
minerals_explored.boron: Associated with lithium deposits and standalone (Piskanja, Jarandol)
minerals_explored.lead_zinc: Traditional Serbian mining commodity (Raska, Trepca belt)
minerals_explored.antimony: Emerging interest (Bindi Metals at Lisa and Mutnica)
minerals_explored.silver: Co-product with lead-zinc and gold deposits

gis_data_sources.note: Official polygon/boundary data for Serbian exploration licenses is maintained by the Ministry of Mining and Energy in their cadastre system. Public GIS access was last updated October 2025. Third-party GIS databases include the BRGM compilation (2002) and various company technical reports (NI 43-101, JORC).

official_cadastre.description: Ministry of Mining and Energy maintains cadastre of exploration spaces and exploitation spaces. GIS system last updated October 2025.

brgm_database.description: BRGM (French Geological Survey) compiled mineral deposits and mining districts of Serbia using MapInfo 6.5 with ArcView 3.2 export. 199 ore deposits across 12 mining districts.
